claims.claim: Evans gates every animation function behind a prefers-reduced-motion media-query check and returns early if the user prefers reduced motion — an accessibility practice any cursor-reactive or animated personal-site feature should copy.

result.summary: The research surfaced three complementary veins of redesign inspiration for frhd.me. First, large quality-filtered seed pools exist for ongoing mining: Awwwards' juried Portfolio Honors archive and its 360-item Freelance Portfolios collection (which isolates pattern-level elements like draggable 3D-polaroid heroes and randomized color-theme switchers with named creators), plus brutalistwebsites.com's ~1,599-entry weird-web directory with ~925 first-person creator interviews. Second, concrete canonical examples were verified in depth: Bruno Simon's bruno-simon.com (navigation as a drivable 3D world with hidden secrets, achievements, a leaderboard, a 30-character multiplayer 'Whispers' system, and humor baked into UI microcopy), Josh Comeau's cursor-reactive rainbow with a hidden configurator whose changes sync to all visitors via PartyKit WebSockets, and Lynn Fisher's 2025 refresh whose signature elastic-resize easter egg and 436px printed-paperback typography show how a fixed editorial layout can hide delight. Third, for the editorial base specifically, gwern.net demonstrates typography-driven devices (sidenotes in margins, three visually distinct link-underline styles with recursive preview popups) built on a no-JS-required progressive-enhancement core that is directly compatible with frhd.me's static-export Next.js architecture. The clearest transferable theme across all verified sites: distinctiveness comes from one committed concept (a world, a book, a rainbow, a margin) plus hidden discoverable layers — exactly the pattern frhd.me's terminal easter egg already starts, and which could be extended with playful microcopy, discovery rewards, and MDX-embedded interactive components in writing posts.

Awwwards 'Honors' selection includes a public voting round atop jury vetting, so 'juried' is a slight simplification. Finally, transferability caveats surfaced by the sources themselves: Josh Comeau's shared-state easter egg required moderation after launch chaos, PartyKit-style real-time sync needs an external service (frhd.me is a static export with no server runtime), and the heavy WebGL/WebGPU approaches (Simon, Samsy) conflict with an editorial site's performance and no-JS-reading budget unless confined to an easter-egg surface like the existing /terminal.
